tldr: The paper investigates whether open-source LLMs can be enhanced to match closed LLM APIs like GPT-4 in tool manipulation with practical human supervision, demonstrating that model alignment with programmatic data, in-context demonstration retrieval, and system prompts can boost open-source LLMs by up to 90%, achieving competitiveness in 4 out of 8 benchmark tasks.
contributions: Identifies three key challenges impeding open-source LLMs in tool manipulation: difficulty in API selection, confusion in populating arguments, and non-executable generation

Adapts three techniques from LLM literature (model alignment with programmatic data, in-context demonstration retriever, system prompt) to enhance open-source LLMs for tool manipulation with minimal human supervision
Introduces ToolBench, the first open-sourced benchmark with pre-defined test cases for quantitative evaluation across 8 diverse tools
Demonstrates that the adapted techniques boost leading open-source LLMs by up to 90% success rate, matching or exceeding GPT-4 in 4 out of 8 tasks
methods: The authors identify three failure modes in open-source LLMs for tool manipulation and propose three corresponding enhancement techniques. First, model alignment via instruction tuning with programmatically generated data: humans curate O(n) templates mapping goal descriptions to API calls, with placeholder pairs filled from candidate value pools. Second, an in-context demonstration retriever module selects semantically similar examples from a human-curated repository of O(n) demonstrations during inference. Third, a system prompt provides inference-time guidelines regulating LLMs to exclusively generate executable API calls in a specific format. They evaluate on ToolBench, a benchmark of 8 tools (2–108 API functions each, ~100 test cases per tool), using success rate as the primary metric.
results: On a weather query tool, GPT-4 achieves 77% success rate while leading open-source LLMs achieve only 19% to 7% success rates (failure rates of 61%–93%). Open-source LLMs show up to 78% lower success rate compared to GPT-4. With all three techniques combined, open-source LLMs improve by up to 90%, attaining results competitive with or better than GPT-4 in 4 out of 8 ToolBench tasks. On the home search task with 15 APIs and only 10 human-curated demonstrations, success rates boost by up to 79% across open-source LLMs, making GPT-4 nearly perfect. On average, one developer day is sufficient to curate templates and demonstrations for one tool.
limitations: Requires human-curated templates and demonstration examples for each tool (though approximately one developer day per tool)
The O(n) demonstration requirement scales with the number of API functions, which can be large for complex tools (up to 108 APIs in Google Sheets)
System prompts and templates are one-time curation tasks and may not generalize to unseen tool types without additional effort
Evaluation is limited to 8 tools in ToolBench, and the approach's scalability to arbitrary new tools is not fully demonstrated
